item.vignette: A 56-year-old man with previously treated Philadelphia chromosome-positive chronic myeloid leukemia in chronic phase receives asciminib. A structural study of the drug-bound BCR::ABL1 kinase shows drug occupancy at a regulatory pocket separate from the ATP-binding site, with reduced kinase activity.
item.lead_in: Which interaction best explains the inhibition?

options.B: Competing with ATP at the ABL nucleotide pocket
options.C: Binding to the BCL-2 hydrophobic groove
options.D: Binding to the extracellular domain of CD20
options.E: Binding to the ABL myristoyl pocket

item.tested_construct: Structural distinction between allosteric ABL inhibition and ATP-competitive inhibition
item.difficulty_basis: Recognize a named allosteric binding site from an explicit structural clue. Author estimate; empirical calibration unavailable.

explanation.key_explanation: Asciminib occupies the ABL myristoyl pocket and inhibits BCR::ABL1 kinase activity. The distinct regulatory site supports allosteric inhibition.

distractor_explanations.A: Proteasome inhibition does not match the structural kinase-binding result.
distractor_explanations.B: The observed binding site is separate from the ATP pocket.
distractor_explanations.C: BCL-2 binding does not explain occupancy of the studied ABL pocket.
distractor_explanations.D: An extracellular antigen target does not explain direct inhibition of the isolated kinase.
distractor_explanations.E: Asciminib occupies the ABL myristoyl pocket and inhibits BCR::ABL1 kinase activity. The distinct regulatory site supports allosteric inhibition.

explanation.educational_objective: Distinguish allosteric kinase inhibition from ATP-site competition.

item.vignette: A 69-year-old woman with relapsed chronic lymphocytic leukemia after a covalent BTK inhibitor begins pirtobrutinib. Her leukemia carries a BTK C481S substitution. In a purified-protein assay, pirtobrutinib inhibits the mutant kinase without formation of a covalent drug-protein adduct.
item.lead_in: Which property accounts for retained inhibition in this assay?

options.A: Recruitment of BTK to an E3 ubiquitin ligase
options.B: Inhibition of BCL-2 rather than binding to BTK
options.C: Noncovalent binding that does not require a cysteine-481 adduct
options.D: Suppression of BTK transcription through promoter methylation
options.E: Covalent attachment requiring the original cysteine at position 481

item.tested_construct: Noncovalent BTK inhibition in a C481-mutant biochemical preparation
item.difficulty_basis: Author estimate of mechanism application; no empirical calibration or discrimination data.

explanation.key_explanation: Pirtobrutinib binds BTK noncovalently and can inhibit forms carrying C481 substitutions. Its binding does not require the missing cysteine adduct.

distractor_explanations.A: The described direct binding assay does not use an E3 ligase or protein-degradation machinery.
distractor_explanations.B: The observed target is isolated BTK, not BCL-2.
distractor_explanations.C: Pirtobrutinib binds BTK noncovalently and can inhibit forms carrying C481 substitutions. Its binding does not require the missing cysteine adduct.
distractor_explanations.D: A purified-protein assay contains no BTK transcriptional process to suppress.
distractor_explanations.E: Serine replaces that cysteine, and no covalent adduct forms.

explanation.educational_objective: Explain how a noncovalent inhibitor can retain activity against a kinase with a covalent-binding-site substitution.

item.vignette: A 64-year-old man with metastatic KRAS G12C-mutated non-small cell lung cancer starts adagrasib after prior systemic therapy. In a protein assay, the drug forms a covalent adduct with the mutant cysteine, and downstream signaling decreases without correction of the KRAS sequence.
item.lead_in: Which change in the mutant protein best accounts for this effect?

options.B: Stabilization of an active signaling state
options.C: Increased exchange into a signaling-active state
options.D: Stabilization of an inactive signaling state
options.E: Increased synthesis of mutant KRAS protein

item.tested_construct: Covalent KRAS G12C inhibition and conformational state
item.difficulty_basis: Author estimate of mechanism application; no empirical calibration or discrimination data.

explanation.key_explanation: Adagrasib covalently binds KRAS G12C and stabilizes its inactive state, limiting downstream signaling without editing the gene.

distractor_explanations.A: Greater effector engagement would not explain the specified inhibition.
distractor_explanations.B: An active state would favor, rather than suppress, signaling.
distractor_explanations.C: Exchange into an active state has the opposite direction of effect.
distractor_explanations.D: Adagrasib covalently binds KRAS G12C and stabilizes its inactive state, limiting downstream signaling without editing the gene.
distractor_explanations.E: Greater protein synthesis is neither the direct binding action nor an explanation for the isolated-protein result.

explanation.educational_objective: Link covalent mutant-protein binding to reduced signaling without genetic correction.

item.vignette: A 30-year-old woman with beta thalassemia requiring regular red-cell transfusions receives luspatercept. In an erythroid-cell model, exposure to the fusion protein reduces excessive SMAD2/3 signaling and promotes late erythroid maturation. A separate receptor assay shows no direct erythropoietin-receptor activation.
item.lead_in: Which extracellular action best explains these findings?

options.C: Sequestration of selected TGF-beta superfamily ligands
options.D: Direct agonism of the erythropoietin receptor
options.E: Binding of the transferrin receptor to increase iron uptake

item.tested_construct: TGF-beta superfamily ligand trapping and erythroid maturation
item.difficulty_basis: Author estimate of mechanism application; no empirical calibration or discrimination data.

explanation.key_explanation: Luspatercept traps selected TGF-beta superfamily ligands, reducing SMAD2/3 signaling and promoting erythroid maturation.

distractor_explanations.A: Iron chelation does not identify the ligand-mediated SMAD2/3 mechanism.
distractor_explanations.B: The identified signaling change is not a consequence of trapping thrombopoietin.
distractor_explanations.C: Luspatercept traps selected TGF-beta superfamily ligands, reducing SMAD2/3 signaling and promoting erythroid maturation.
distractor_explanations.D: The separate assay excludes direct erythropoietin-receptor agonism.
distractor_explanations.E: Increasing iron uptake does not match the fusion protein’s documented ligand-binding action.

explanation.educational_objective: Distinguish promotion of erythroid maturation through ligand trapping from erythropoietin-receptor agonism.

item.vignette: A 41-year-old woman with a progressing desmoid tumor requiring systemic therapy begins nirogacestat. item.tested_construct: Proteolytic Notch activation versus downstream signal termination
item.difficulty_basis: Author estimate of mechanism application; no empirical calibration or discrimination data.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize proteolytic receptor activation as a signaling step that can be pharmacologically blocked.

item.vignette: A 58-year-old man with advanced systemic mastocytosis receives avapritinib. His mast cells carry KIT D816V. In a ligand-free cell assay, the cells show constitutive KIT autophosphorylation; drug exposure reduces this phosphorylation while total KIT protein and the mutant sequence remain unchanged.
item.lead_in: Which action most directly explains the result?

options.A: Inhibition of mutant KIT kinase activity
options.E: Neutralization of extracellular stem cell factor

item.tested_construct: Direct inhibition of ligand-independent mutant KIT signaling
item.difficulty_basis: Identify direct kinase inhibition from a ligand-free phosphorylation experiment. Author estimate; empirical calibration unavailable.

explanation.key_explanation: Avapritinib inhibits KIT D816V kinase activity. Reduced autophosphorylation can occur without removing the receptor or repairing its sequence.

distractor_explanations.A: Avapritinib inhibits KIT D816V kinase activity. Reduced autophosphorylation can occur without removing the receptor or repairing its sequence.
distractor_explanations.B: IgE neutralization does not explain direct suppression of the constitutively active kinase.
distractor_explanations.C: Leukotriene synthesis is not the measured receptor-kinase event.
distractor_explanations.D: Histamine-receptor blockade does not directly inhibit KIT autophosphorylation.
distractor_explanations.E: No ligand is present, so ligand neutralization cannot explain the observed inhibition.

explanation.educational_objective: Distinguish inhibition of an oncogenic kinase from blockade of mast-cell mediators.

item.vignette: A 67-year-old woman with relapsed multiple myeloma after four prior treatment lines, including a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory agent, and an anti-CD38 antibody, receives teclistamab monotherapy. In coculture, the antibody promotes T-cell-dependent myeloma-cell lysis. Preventing antibody binding to BCMA abolishes this effect.
item.lead_in: Which pair of cell-surface targets enables this interaction?

options.A: CD28 on T cells and BCMA on myeloma cells
options.B: CD3 on T cells and CD20 on myeloma cells
options.C: CD16 on natural killer cells and CD38 on myeloma cells
options.D: CD3 on T cells and BCMA on myeloma cells
options.E: PD-1 on T cells and PD-L1 on myeloma cells

item.tested_construct: Bispecific CD3-BCMA T-cell engagement
item.difficulty_basis: Author estimate of mechanism application; no empirical calibration or discrimination data.

explanation.key_explanation: Teclistamab is bispecific for CD3 and BCMA, linking T-cell engagement to recognition of BCMA-expressing cells.

distractor_explanations.A: BCMA is correct, but the T-cell binding target is CD3 rather than CD28.
distractor_explanations.B: This pair does not include the required BCMA target.
distractor_explanations.C: This describes a different effector-cell and antigen pairing, not the stated T-cell interaction.
distractor_explanations.D: Teclistamab is bispecific for CD3 and BCMA, linking T-cell engagement to recognition of BCMA-expressing cells.
distractor_explanations.E: Checkpoint blockade is not the demonstrated CD3-BCMA bridging mechanism.

explanation.educational_objective: Explain how a bispecific antibody couples an effector T cell to a tumor-associated antigen.

distractor_explanations.E: Increased opsonization has the wrong direction for proximal alternative-pathway inhibition.

explanation.educational_objective: Connect proximal alternative-pathway inhibition to both opsonization and terminal complement effects.

item.vignette: A 5-year-old child with nephropathic cystinosis receives delayed-release cysteamine. In affected cells, lysosomal cystine decreases after drug exposure even though the inherited cystine-transport defect remains. Cysteine and a cysteine-cysteamine mixed disulfide appear and can leave the lysosome.
item.lead_in: Which process explains the reduction in stored cystine?

options.A: Increased glomerular filtration of intact lysosomal cystine
options.C: Thiol-disulfide exchange generating products that can exit the lysosome
options.D: Correction of the defective transporter’s gene
options.E: Inhibition of cellular protein uptake as the primary action

item.tested_construct: Chemical bypass of defective lysosomal cystine transport
item.difficulty_basis: Author estimate of mechanism application; no empirical calibration or discrimination data.

explanation.key_explanation: Cysteamine chemically converts cystine through thiol-disulfide exchange into cysteine and a mixed disulfide that can leave the lysosome.

distractor_explanations.A: A cellular lysosomal experiment is not explained by a renal filtration process.
distractor_explanations.B: Transport remains defective; the reaction instead generates different products that can exit.
distractor_explanations.C: Cysteamine chemically converts cystine through thiol-disulfide exchange into cysteine and a mixed disulfide that can leave the lysosome.
distractor_explanations.D: The transporter defect remains in the experiment.
distractor_explanations.E: The identified products support direct chemical conversion rather than simply less substrate entry.

explanation.educational_objective: Explain depletion of a stored metabolite without restoration of its defective transporter.

item.lead_in: Which explanation best accounts for the platform-dependent discrepancy?

options.A: Biotin competition within the assay capture system
options.B: Interference by the therapeutic enzyme with the detection reaction
options.D: Cross-reactivity from newly accumulated hormone fragments
options.E: Heterophile antibody bridging of assay antibodies

item.tested_construct: Therapeutic alkaline phosphatase and analytical assay interference
item.difficulty_basis: Author estimate of mechanism application; no empirical calibration or discrimination data.

explanation.key_explanation: Asfotase alfa can interfere with ALP-conjugated laboratory assays. Reproducing the effect by adding the purified drug supports analytical interference rather than a true hormone change.

distractor_explanations.A: Biotin is absent, and adding the therapeutic enzyme reproduces the effect.
distractor_explanations.B: Asfotase alfa can interfere with ALP-conjugated laboratory assays. Reproducing the effect by adding the purified drug supports analytical interference rather than a true hormone change.
distractor_explanations.C: The control lacks patient autoantibodies.

distractor_explanations.E: Patient immunoglobulins are absent from the defined control.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize therapeutic-enzyme interference as a cause of platform-dependent laboratory results.
